reason: The cited evidence supports that thermo-mechanical processing (cold rolling + annealing) can produce heterogeneous microstructures with strength-ductility synergy in HEAs (E3), and that coherent precipitates can strengthen without large ductility loss (E2). However, no evidence is provided for cryo-rolling specifically, for the claimed improvements in Young’s modulus or fracture resistance, or for the specific annealing window of 800–900°C producing the exact dual-phase architecture described.
premises: Cryo-rolling introduces high dislocation density and nucleation sites for recrystallization/precipitation
Controlled annealing (800–900°C) triggers partial recrystallization and coherent nanoprecipitate formation
Coherent, low-misfit precipitates strengthen without severely compromising ductility
Heterogeneous ultrafine grain + precipitate microstructure enhances work hardening via GNDs and back stress
This microstructure improves Young’s modulus and fracture resistance
